note: A regional workshop report (Cotonou, 11-14 October 2021); for Mauritania it gives only a national DGI system and tablet-based fiscal census, with no commune-run payer and payment record or count of communes, so no revenue-class fact.

facts.fact: In Sebkha, a seven-week census of taxpayers found 10,564 taxpayers instead of the 2,000 officially recognised; the El Mouhassil software, launched in April 2019, issues numbered barcoded fiscal stamps, tracks each stamp from stock to sale to its payment into the commune's Treasury account, and 13 agents with tablets cover 16 sectors and scan each trader's stamp for paid, paid-this-month or overdue status.
The Sebkha mayor describes the system as completely independent, run by the commune with its own stamps; the trace is lost when the money enters the commune's account at the Public Treasury.

El Mouhassil is live in one commune, Sebkha (Nouakchott), since April 2019; eight others are installing it in April 2020: Tevragh Zeina, Timbedra, Nouadhibou, Boghé, Ksar, Toujounine, Arafat and Rosso; no national count of communes is given.
The commune's mayor defined the management processes and entrusted the build to a Mauritanian start-up; the commune runs the system and thanks German cooperation (GIZ) for technical expertise.
GIZ provided technical expertise to the commune for El Mouhassil; no commune budget line for it is stated.

Collection with the new secured fiscal stamps resumed in Sebkha in January 2020; the piece reports a 500 per cent rise in communal taxes between 2018 and 2020 and installation under way in eight more communes (April 2020).

facts.fact: Mauritania's decentralisation directorate says the municipal collector application, in use since 2020, now benefits about 30 municipalities and will be extended to the rest.
The Interior Ministry's decentralisation directorate organised the workshop validating the user guide of the El Mouhassil municipal collector system.
The Mudun project, supported by the World Bank, has funded training, equipment, technical support and collectors' bonuses for El Mouhassil in municipalities.

systems.owner: Ministry of Interior, Directorate General of Decentralisation

facts.fact: The mayor of Ksar says the El Mouhassil programme runs a full taxpayer census whose data go into the municipal database, with the commune's office then applying council decisions on the municipal tax, set on 14 criteria per taxpayer.
The mayor says the census data are entered in the Ksar municipal database, managed by an office the commune created.

El Mouhassil was developed in cooperation between Mauritania's Ministry of the Interior and Decentralisation and German cooperation, and adopted by the commune of Ksar with several other municipalities cooperating.
